Joining us are Elon Musk, Chief Executive Officer, and Vaibhav Taneja, Chief Financial Officer. VAIBHAV TANEJA (CFO), PREPARED REMARKS: Total revenue for the first quarter was 21.3 billion dollars, down 9 percent year over year. Automotive revenue declined 13 percent year over year, driven by lower average selling prices and lower deliveries. We delivered 386,810 vehicles in the quarter and produced 433,371, so we built meaningfully more than we delivered and inventory increased. Several factors weighed on the quarter: the early ramp of the updated Model 3 at Fremont, factory shutdowns from shipping diversions in the Red Sea, and the arson attack that halted production at Gigafactory Berlin. Operating income was 1.2 billion dollars and operating margin was 5.5 percent, down year over year. GAAP net income was 1.1 billion dollars. Free cash flow was negative 2.5 billion dollars in the quarter, reflecting a 2.7 billion dollar increase in inventory and 1.0 billion dollars of AI infrastructure capital expenditure. Energy storage deployments reached a record 4.1 gigawatt hours, and energy generation and storage gross margin reached a record. Services and Other revenue grew 25 percent year over year. On the outlook, we are between two major growth waves. We expect the vehicle volume growth rate in 2024 to be notably lower than the growth rate achieved in 2023. We are updating our future vehicle lineup to accelerate the launch of new models ahead of our previously communicated start of production in the second half of 2025. ELON MUSK (CEO), PREPARED REMARKS: Regarding the product roadmap, we have updated our plan to accelerate the launch of new models. These will use aspects of the next generation platform as well as aspects of our current platforms, and will be produced on the same manufacturing lines as our current lineup. This is more capital efficient than building entirely new lines. On autonomy, we recently released a version of Full Self-Driving that is a significant improvement. We are also in discussions with a major automaker about licensing FSD. Energy storage will grow much faster than the automotive business. We think the stationary storage business is going to be extremely large. QUESTION AND ANSWER SESSION ANALYST, DEUTSCHE BANK: Can you clarify the timing on the new models? ELON MUSK: We expect to begin production of new models in early 2025, possibly late this year. That is ahead of the prior plan. ANALYST, WEDBUSH: How should we think about margins from here? VAIBHAV TANEJA: Pricing remains a challenge. We expect continued pressure on automotive gross margin in the near term as we balance volume and price. We are focused on cost reduction per vehicle, which declined again this quarter. ANALYST, MORGAN STANLEY: What is the capital commitment to AI? ELON MUSK: We expect capital expenditures to exceed 10 billion dollars this year, with a substantial portion going to AI compute. We are installing significant training capacity. That said, I want to be clear that this is a large spend and it does compress near-term free cash flow. ANALYST, CANACCORD: Any comment on demand in China? VAIBHAV TANEJA: The market there is highly competitive and price competition has intensified. We continue to see pressure on pricing across the region. OPERATOR: That concludes today's call. Thank you.

CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. We will finish strong. Vladimir, any closing remarks? VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): First, thank you for all the engagement from institutional, sell-side, retail, and content creators. I am proud of the community that has coalesced around the company. The team has been working incredibly hard. The roadmap is full and there is a lot to do. I hope to see some of you at the next Hood Summit in Houston, Texas. Thank you.

CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): Thank you to everyone for joining Robinhood's Q2 2026 earnings call, whether you are tuning into the livestream or here with us in person. With us today are Chairman and CEO, Vladimir Tenev; CFO, Shiv Kumar Verma; and VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations, Chris Koegel. Vladimir and Shiv will offer opening remarks and then open the call to Q&A. During the Q&A portion of the call, we will answer questions from the audience, which includes institutional research analysts, finance content creators who may hold an ownership position in Robinhood, and both institutional and retail shareholders. As a reminder, today's call will contain forward-looking statements. Actual results could differ materially from our current expectations and we may not provide updates unless legally required. Potential risk factors that could cause differences, including regulatory developments that we continue to monitor, are described in the press release we issued today, the earnings presentation, and our SEC filings, all of which can be found at investors.robinhood.com. Today's discussion will also include non-GAAP financial measures. Reconciliations to the GAAP measures we consider most directly comparable can be found in the earnings presentation. With that, please welcome Vladimir and Shiv.
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): Wow. Thank you, everyone, for joining. Thanks for the warm welcome, and it is awesome to see a packed house here. We are back again at NASDAQ in New York City, taking a big bite out of the Big Apple with Shiv here and Chris. This is our largest audience yet for an earnings event. I remember last year when we did the first event with analysts in person, we were worried: would anyone come? Not too many did then, but the people that did had a lot of fun. Now I am glad to see the word has spread. So it is really great to see shareholders, analysts, buy side and sell side, and content creators in the audience. It has been about five years, I think exactly five years, since we rang the bell at NASDAQ. In that time, we have accomplished significant growth and delivered for our customers. Since the IPO, total platform assets have quadrupled and adjusted EBITDA has more than 8x. But one thing has not changed: why we exist. Robinhood exists to make everyone an owner, and I think that is a unique vision. Not many companies are going after this. It is a powerful vision, not just for each individual customer, but also for society at large. A society without broadly distributed ownership is fragile. We think broad ownership is essential to a free, stable, and prosperous society. When more people have a stake in the outcome, more skin in the game, they are literally invested in the outcome, and we want more people to be invested in the companies of our great country. I think we have just scratched the surface of what we can do. To achieve our aspirations of making everyone an owner, we are focused on three things. Number one: being number one in active traders, which will allow customers to own any tradable asset. Number two: being the leader in wallet for the next generation, bringing ownership to the entire family—lifelong ownership. Number three: building the leading global financial ecosystem, which is about expanding ownership that we have contributed to in the U.S. worldwide. Billions of people around the world could benefit. In Q2, our continued product velocity across these three arcs led to a bunch of records. On the active trader front, the core business is humming, which drove market share gains and record volumes across equities, options, and prediction markets in the quarter. I have to highlight: Rothera started supporting Robinhood prediction markets and has rapidly become a top three designated contract market in the U.S. We also launched the first version of Agentic trading, which allows customers to build AI agents to trade equities, options, and crypto and to have access to Robinhood tools and features. We are very excited about that. Looking at wallet share, trust accounts have officially launched, a historic step toward enabling broad financial ownership from birth. We are honored to serve as broker and sole initial trustee, helping millions of American children become owners of our economy from day one. We also crossed an exciting milestone for the Robinhood Gold Card: one million cardholders. That is a number we are very excited about. The Gold Card is now driving over $17 billion in annualized purchase volume — it is being heavily used. Plus, we broke $3 billion in banking deposits since we began rolling out just last November. All this put together contributed to record net deposits. Customers are continuing to trust us with more and more of their assets, which in turn helped drive total platform assets to record levels in the quarter as well. Finally, on the global financial ecosystem, we closed our acquisition of WonderFi in Canada. We received our capital markets services license in Singapore. At our crypto and international event 'The World is Flat,' we introduced a suite of products including Robinhood Chain, which is the first chain purpose-built for real world assets. We have seen a lot of great initial traction on these products, particularly the chain: over $12 billion in DEX volume after launch, making it one of the largest chains by transaction volume over the past week. It was the fastest chain to get to 100 million transactions; we are well north of 150 million transactions at this point, which is very cool. Also, customers have deposited over $200 million into Robinhood Earn. Remember, Robinhood Earn is our stablecoin lending product powered by Robinhood Chain and our stablecoin USDG, and it allows customers to earn 7% APY, which is a competitive rate. So $200 million so far in just a few weeks. Stock tokens are perhaps the thing I am most excited about. We are very excited about bringing ownership of real world assets to everyone in the world. Stock tokens are available in more than 120 countries, which allow many people around the globe to experience the idea of ownership. Tokenization makes it possible to expand exposure to high-quality assets like U.S. stocks to every single person with an Internet connection. If you have a smartphone and Internet, you can connect to our blockchain and get exposure to U.S. stocks. We are now serving over one million accounts outside the U.S. and are very much at the beginning there. Overall, continued product velocity across these three arcs led to record results in Q2: record revenues of $1.3 billion, up 32% from last year; record net deposits of $22 billion, which is a 28% annualized growth rate; and record Gold subscribers of 4.8 million, which is now a 17% attach rate relative to our net funded accounts. Now I will hand it over to Shiv to discuss our results in more detail. Shiv?
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): All right. Well, thanks, Vladimir. Before getting to the results, I wanted to share three big takeaways from the quarter. First, the core business is going strong. Net deposits were a record $22 billion, a 28% growth rate, and we drove new records across equities, options, prediction markets, and margin. It is also great to see top-of-funnel growth picked up as we added nearly one million funded customers in the quarter. Second, this led to both record revenues, up 32% year over year, and another quarter of strong profitability with 57% adjusted EBITDA margins. We are continuing to drive strong top-line growth and profitability at scale. Lastly, we are dialed in on expenses. We are lowering and tightening our outlook even as our core businesses grew to new highs and we layered on new products. Let's review Q2 results compared to a year ago. Revenues grew 32% to a record $1.3 billion, driven by strong growth across the business. Transaction volumes increased to record levels across the majority of our asset classes, and we drove market share to new highs. Interest-earning assets also grew: we had records across margin, our credit card book, and Robinhood Banking. Other revenues were up as Gold subscribers reached an all-time high of 4.8 million and we started monetizing revenues from our work on the trust accounts. While product velocity continues to increase and revenues continue to grow to new highs, we also stayed disciplined on cost. Adjusted OpEx and SBC was $641 million as we managed expenses well below our prior outlook range, all while including costs related to two new businesses, Rothera and WonderFi, that were not included in our prior outlook. Looking to the rest of the year, while we are adding costs related to Rothera and WonderFi, we are getting even more efficient in how we operate. This is allowing us to both self-fund Rothera and WonderFi costs and remove additional costs from the system. So we are lowering and tightening our 2026 outlook for adjusted OpEx and SBC to a range of $2.675 billion to $2.775 billion. We believe it is a competitive advantage to not only be a growth company that can invest for the long term, but also to leverage our lean and disciplined operating model to self-fund a meaningful amount of these new investments. Taken together, the strong top-line growth and expense discipline we drove in Q2 flowed to the bottom line. Adjusted EBITDA was $741 million, up 35% year over year, and a 57% margin. Earnings per share was $0.62, up 48% year over year. If we turn to capital allocation, a few items are top of mind. In June, we opportunistically raised $2.2 billion of capital to give us even more flexibility to invest for future growth. We believe we have a massive opportunity ahead of us, and the capital gives us even more capacity to go after it. We raised this capital on attractive terms for shareholders with a 0% coupon and no net dilution until our share price exceeds $300. Even while raising capital, we are prudently managing our share count. Year-to-date, we have repurchased 7.5 million shares for $664 million. Denominator matters. Overall, we are proud of the results we drove in Q2, and Q3 is also off to a good start. July average daily volumes compared to a record Q2 are in a similar area for equities, options, and event contracts. July net deposits are tracking toward the $4 billion area, and this does not yet include deposits into the trust accounts. Stepping back, we feel great about the products we are shipping and the growth we are driving, but we've heard from some investors that it can be difficult to know which growth areas to focus on. So I wanted to share three areas we think are important for measuring progress and success on our long-term vision. First, net deposits: customers continue to trust us with their hard-earned deposits at over 20% growth rates. As we drive strong net deposit growth, assets compound, and this leads to strong business growth. Second, rule of 40: we are driving double-digit revenue growth with strong adjusted EBITDA margins — a combination that has made us more than a rule of 80 company in the past few years. We think it is important to be both a growth company and a company that operates with strong margins, and all of this at our scale of over $5 billion of annual revenue is quite rare. Third, $100 million ARR businesses: we are now up to 13 businesses that have reached this level as we rapidly ship for customers, including two new ones added this quarter: Robinhood Lending and the credit card. As we build out a family of financial apps, we plan to add even more $100 million ARR businesses in the year to come. If we keep making progress on these areas quarter after quarter, year after year, the financial results should follow. Our financial north star remains the same: maximize earnings per share and free cash flow per share for shareholders over time. Before we move to Q&A, I am going to turn it back over to Vladimir to show us a few of these great products that we recently built. Vladimir?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): Thanks, Shiv. I want to try something a little different, if I may. Many of you are probably familiar with our main app, but over the past few years we have expanded from a single trading app to a broader system. I want to give you a little tour of some of the other family of apps that we have built and improved very recently. Here they are: our four apps. I will not show the main one, but let us start with this one here: trust accounts. This has been an incredible collaboration between Treasury and the National Design Studio, Robinhood teams, and BNY. I believe it is the best digital experience the government has ever delivered. The Secretary said this was like the best product launch the government has ever done, which is high praise. This is my kids' trust account. One of the things we have done well is showing the magic of compound interest front and center. You not only see the account values today, but you can see what happens by age 18 and simulate if you add $50 or $130 per month what you can expect by age 18. You can even extend it to age 60 for retirement. We wanted to illustrate how magical compounding is and get people thinking long term. You can scroll down and get a feeling for the companies in the low-cost ETFs. My favorite feature is contribution flow: we have an illustration and make it super easy to contribute. If you want to do $5, my Robinhood checking account is linked and there is a coin animation that fills up your piggy bank. You can make it a recurring contribution. The level of the coins corresponds exactly to how close you are to your annual giving limit of $5,000. You can share via a QR code or link; folks can contribute without even having an account through Apple Pay. There is educational content to learn the basics about the stock market and investing. We think it can be a great charitable giving vehicle; Michael Dell and many others have already given. We are working to make it easy for employers to donate — there is a $2,500 tax-free employer limit per year which Robinhood is participating in. If you do not have it, I recommend picking it up for your children or grandchildren. Expect it to continue to get better. Take a look at the banking app. We believe we are building the best digital banking experience in the market. You can see the premium art deco feel; we wanted a banking experience with no compromises. Neo banks usually have sacrifices, but we want a true private banking product. One thing customers love is the APY. You can earn high APYs on both checking and savings just by setting up direct deposit and being a Gold subscriber — no minimums. We give you 3.5% automatically on every account and customers love it. About 40% of customers are signed up for direct deposit, which is a great attach rate. We redesigned the rewards menu to make it easier to access. You can get 3% cash back, upgrade to the Gold Card, and access many reward redemptions. The family tab lets you add family members — this is the first banking product where family is a first-class citizen. Customers direct deposit into banking, can spend with their credit card, and cash back flows back into brokerage, which turbocharges investing. Also, we just started rolling out the Platinum card and it is looking really good; we have iterated on feedback from the launch. Now the Robinhood wallet. As part of 'The World is Flat' announcements, we launched Robinhood Chain Mainnet. A robust chain like Robinhood Chain needs a robust wallet. I will caveat that many features I will show are not available in the U.S.; they are ex-U.S. products available in over 120 countries. You will see similar design language but everything is powered by crypto technology. One of the tabs is perpetual futures. The wallet is well integrated into Robinhood Chain. Through our partnership with Leiter, active traders outside the U.S. can get leveraged exposure to crypto perps, commodity perps, and single-stock perps as well. We make it easy to add funds, deposit and withdraw, and place trades. I am very excited about stock tokens. Here is NVIDIA: if you are a customer outside the U.S., you can get exposure to NVIDIA through stock tokens. They have advantages over traditional stocks: tradable 24/7 including weekends and holidays, and you can send them on-chain. This makes it easy to expand ownership worldwide — all you need is an Internet connection. We will continue to add lots more stocks and push tokenization of other real world assets. We have momentum and more products in the pipeline. We have our third annual Hood Summit in a couple months, 'The Engines of Creation' live from Houston, Texas. With that, Chris, unless you want me to show more apps, we can go to Q&A.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): Thank you very much, Vladimir and Shiv. For the Q&A session, we will start by answering shareholder questions from Say Technologies. After the Say questions, we will turn to live questions from our audience and then to dial-in participants. I am going to kick it off with our first question from Say. Zach, are you joining us?
ZACH (Shareholder / Content Creator): Hello? Do you guys hear me? Hey, everyone. Happy to be here. Just wanted to know, what is the goal of Robinhood Social and when will it go live to the general public?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): Thanks for the question. I noticed you are on Robinhood Social, if I am not mistaken, and there was some discussion on Robinhood Social about this question. The goal with Robinhood Social is to help customers learn from one another. Robinhood has largely been a tool to place trades, but the idea for trades typically came from outside. We asked ourselves: can we help customers learn from one another and take advantage of the large community we've built to support idea generation? So far, we are seeing great early signs. One advantage we have compared to other social platforms is that we have trading data, so we can validate claims: when someone says they made a trade, we can confirm it and show the portfolio they claim to have. We are adding features and tuning the feed ranking algorithm before rolling it out broadly. The goal is to get it out to everyone by the end of the quarter. We are iterating and making sure functionality in posts is tuned before general availability. We like what we are seeing and feel pretty good about rolling it out before the end of the quarter. Thank you.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Thank you for your question, Zach. Next question is coming from John.
JOHN (Analyst): Hey, all. Hey, Shiv and Vladimir. Thanks for taking my question. Mine's on the Clarity Act, and I understand it is still moving through the Senate so things could change. But could you give an idea of what would be the most impactful aspects of that to Robinhood if something similar were to pass, and if there are delays, any impacts as well?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): I will take that one. The Clarity Act is very important because while the current administration has been crypto-forward, we want the industry's foundation in the U.S. to be durable. We do not want the rules to shift every four or eight years. Regulatory stability is necessary for the industry to grow, and that happens through legislation. We saw progress with other legislation previously; Clarity takes it a step further. One area we've been pushing hard on is tokenization. We have been investing in our tokenized offerings and believe this will be a big industry. We are pushing tokenization outside the U.S. already, and we've seen advantages from v1 to v2 of our tokenized products: fully on-chain, 24/7 trading, send and receive, and fractionalization by default. It would be a shame if the U.S. did not benefit from these advantages. Clarity helps take us a step further. We are not standing still: we are pushing on both on-chain and traditional centralized products and innovating overseas in some areas. With Robinhood Earn and other on-chain products in the U.S., we think we will be good regardless, but clarity will be very important to realizing the full potential of these products.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Thanks, John. The last question from Say comes from Joe.
JOE (Shareholder / Say Technologies Participant): Can you give us an update on early traction with trust accounts since the July launch? Specifically the number of accounts opened, assets flowing in, and how you are thinking about long-term contributions to net deposits and assets under custody?
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): Great question. We have been very pleased with the progress thus far. Seven million children have signed up and we've seen nearly $1.5 billion in contributions into trust accounts already, and that is before a lot of the philanthropic contributions have started flowing in. We think this will get to tens of millions, and we are working aggressively to do that. We believe it will continue to grow very rapidly from here.
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): It will take continued hard work. Programs that have success lead to demand for more features. With our partners, we are working hard to deliver: on direct deposit so employers can fund trust accounts for employees, and making a great philanthropic experience. Right now the options for charitable giving are not great — there is no default low-cost option. We can provide a default, great, low-cost mechanism, and we are excited. This is just the beginning.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. That concludes the Say portion of our Q&A. We are now going to Q&A from our live audience. We ask that each person limit their questions to one. Please raise your hand if you would like to ask a question. Can we get the mic to Dan Dolev?
DAN DOLEV (Analyst (Mizuho)): Hi. Dan Dolev at Mizuho. Congrats, Vladimir and Shiv. Amazing quarter. What surprised us the most on the positive side was the amazing growth in funded accounts. Could you shed some light on what part of that is structural, what you are doing, and maybe a quick update on progress in Europe and how that is going? Very impressive, thank you.
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): I am happy to start with that one. We said last quarter we were making a concerted effort at top-of-funnel, and it is great to see progress. The million funded customers added is the most we have added in a quarter in nearly five years since the IPO. There were a variety of things, not any one single driver: a strong macro market backdrop helped, and many new products came out, including banking and the credit card, which contributed strong organic growth. The SpaceX IPO helped and we had an acquisition in the quarter that provided a couple hundred thousand accounts. We continue to grow overseas. This quarter showed the power of the ecosystem and financial apps Vladimir discussed. Multiple vectors were growing simultaneously. We will keep focusing on top-of-funnel through new products and marketing; it will be one of our top KPIs going forward.
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): More to do. The team is energized.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): Moving from the front row to the second row, Daniel Fannon.
DANIEL FANNON (Analyst): Thanks. I wanted to talk about prediction markets and how you are thinking about sustainability as we exit events like the World Cup and bridge to football season. How do you think about the long-term durability of this asset class and what you are seeing outside of sports, such as macro or bigger events?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): The great thing about prediction markets is there are events all the time: football season, midterms, and many other predictable and unpredictable events. Customers will want to trade and hedge their portfolios. We are gearing up for that and making continuous product and pricing improvements. Rothera has gone live and the World Cup was a proof of concept. We are looking to scale rapidly and provide great pricing to our customers by routing to multiple venues so customers get the best deal possible on Robinhood.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Next, David Smith.
DAVID SMITH (Analyst): Thank you. In the past you said new customers often come to Robinhood for one product and adopt more over time. With the strong prediction market engagement in June and continuing into July, can you help us understand how much of that came from existing prediction markets users, existing Robinhood customers new to prediction markets, and new customers who joined Robinhood recently to transact in this product?
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): Happy to take that. When people come to Robinhood to do one thing, they tend to do more. New customers still sign up for Gold at about 40% to 50% attach in many cases, so customers come for equities, prediction markets, crypto, or banking and discover Gold and other products. Regardless of entry point, they tend to adopt additional products. Prediction markets customers are actually more likely to have a retirement account with Robinhood. The last number we shared was about 1.5 million people used prediction markets; that number is now closer to 2 million. Growth has been broad across products and customers are adopting multiple products at the same time.
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): On marketing, we continue to see strong ROIs across prediction markets, Gold, and active trader offerings. We are benefiting from multiple fronts working well simultaneously.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Let's next go to Devin Ryan in the front row.
DEVIN RYAN (Analyst (Citizens)): Thanks. You mentioned version one of Agentic. Can you talk about what you are learning from customers using it, how investment performance has been, interesting behaviors, and how that maps to version 2.0? When will broader capabilities come to all customers?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): Since we are the first major platform doing this, we started conservatively: stocks first and separate Agentic accounts. Customers typically fund with a relatively small amount and link their agent. We have expanded to allow options in Agentic accounts as well. Customers have done interesting things, putting together complex strategies. Crypto is coming soon. Over 100,000 people have integrated and opened Agentic accounts, which has been great. AUM and trading volumes for Agentic have been growing. One piece of friction is that not everyone loves going to a code editor or stitching together apps like Claude — it requires sophistication. Also, some models are not familiar with trading and can resist being used for trading; they may say they do not want to trade. We are addressing ease-of-use and model behavior, and we are hard at work on improvements.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Next, Christian Blue.
CHRISTIAN BLUE (Analyst (Autonomous)): Christian Blue with Autonomous. You called out Rothera as a top three DCM. How do you see your vision around having a DCM and retail distribution evolving? Is there a possibility to build that out into perps or traditional futures to challenge the top designated contract markets?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): We are top three after one month but are not satisfied. The road map for Rothera — a joint venture — is to grow and add more capabilities. They are focused now on prediction markets and event contracts, but over time you should see expansion. We also have perps overseas through Bitstamp and other venues where we have been increasing scope, now offering commodity perps and expecting inventory expansion over time. Our goal is to give Robinhood customers access to the best products from multiple exchange providers and to make costs clear and low for customers. This will be multi-homed and could become a B2B business over time; right now we are focused on delivering a great retail experience.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): Ramsey, could you take the mic next?
RAMSEY EL-ASSAL (Analyst (Cantor)): Hi. Ramsey El-Assal from Cantor. Now that Robinhood Chain is live, how should we think about the broader DeFi roadmap? You have tokenized assets, Robinhood Earn, perps in the wallet. What other on-chain services could be next — lending and borrowing, other yield-generating products?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): We already have lending and borrowing available through partners; developers are building interesting things. The big thing is developer momentum: because of the volume, many wallets and protocols integrated quickly, which attracts more developers. We have been among the top chains in developer activity. Developers are building things that compose with real world assets — RWAs — in ways we had not thought of. Our roadmap is to improve infrastructure, APIs, and block speed, and add more RWAs and stock tokens. Our unique contribution is supplying RWAs as a key primitive of the chain and making sure they work well for developers to compose on top of.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Next question: James Yaro has his hand up.
JAMES YARO (Analyst (Goldman Sachs)): James Yarrow, Goldman Sachs. Regarding perps in the U.S.: what is the appetite to add them into the U.S. brokerage? What are the hurdles to rolling them out and are you looking to roll them out in the near term, CFTC approval permitting?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): We have been in conversations with the CFTC and they have been constructive. We are making progress. I do not have specific timing to share, but we feel good about customers having a great perps experience. We already have perps in Europe, so the work is not a large amount of engineering effort. I would not interpret absence of a near-term timeline here as lack of intent; we intend to be aggressive but avoid giving specific timelines on an earnings call.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Next question from Daniel with Crossroads.
DANIEL (Analyst): Hi. Are there plans to add support for foreign stocks? Right now investors have to buy ETFs to get exposure to certain foreign companies.
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): Yes, in short, yes. It is on our roadmap. Over time, we want to provide U.S. stocks to customers worldwide and foreign stocks to customers worldwide, including in the U.S. We will build out a marketplace. Our common infrastructure can be a real asset there. It's not something that happens instantly — it requires regional connections and licensure — but it is top of mind and will be a focus.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Please pass the mic to the right and back one row. Thank you. John from Artemis up next.
JOHN (Analyst (Artemis)): John from Artemis. Congrats on Robinhood Chain: $15 billion of monthly trading volume, two-plus million monthly transacting users, and $500 million of stablecoin supply. What could go right with Robinhood Chain? You could offer an opportunity of having the Robinhood app to everyone globally — what could go right?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): A lot could go right. We built Robinhood Chain to be purpose-built for real world assets. Our unique contribution is RWAs. We are doing the difficult work on liquidity and regulatory side to safely bring these assets on-chain and make them useful. We started with stock tokens and will grow them and make them fully DeFi-enabled. We are adding other types of RWAs and seeing developers build interesting products. Our job is to give developers better tools and infrastructure. Enthusiasm has been great, but we know there is more to do and we must keep building to be the most useful chain for developers and traders.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Next, Craig Maurer.
CRAIG MAURER (Analyst (FT Partners)): Hi, Craig Maurer with FT Partners. You disclosed in the deck that you are trending toward roughly $4 billion in net deposits for July, which is down from June and the lowest of the year. Any commentary around that? Does it have anything to do with the drawdown in semiconductors and what is happening in the market?
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): Great question. Our goal remains about 20% net deposit growth on an annual basis. I do not read too much into any particular month or quarter. Year-to-date including July, we are still well north of 20%. Q2 was really strong and engagement will fluctuate: macro, product launches, seasonality — summer tends to be a bit slower, and promotions vary. What we are focused on is continuing to deliver for customers and adding durable engines of net deposit growth. The health of our customers looks very strong: engagement is solid and customers tend to buy on down days, which we saw in Q2. July average daily volumes are similar to Q2 average and net deposits are strong. Everything we are seeing suggests customer health is strong.
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): We also see long-term tailwinds to deposit growth: banking is an early success and still early in integration; advisor network and RIA integration can be durable sources of deposits; trusts are rolling out and that can attract higher-net-worth deposits. As we add and support these features, they should be long-term durable tailwinds for net deposit growth.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Craig, please pass the mic up one row to Alexander.
ALEXANDER (Analyst (Button)): Hi. Alexander with Button. Peter Thiel said going from $100 billion to a trillion would be significantly harder. As Robinhood approaches $100 billion market cap, how do you think about the difficulty of the next 10x? Could getting to a trillion be easier because of scale and operating leverage? What will it take for Robinhood to surpass market caps of legacy financial institutions, and do you see AI supercharging global plans?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): Getting to a trillion will be very difficult, but I think it can be done. It is not just growing brokerage internationally; it's also agentic finance, making tools that could move a lot of activity into agents, Robinhood Chain enabling many people globally to access U.S. assets, private markets, and more. Robinhood Ventures and our fund activity aim to give individual investors access to companies at the earliest stages across the lifecycle. I see multiple axes that could 10x the company and we will pursue them.
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): We do not comment on the stock price specifically, but we have said we believe we can 10x the business over the next ten years through these vectors. Assets are the greatest predictor of financial performance. We are nearly $400 billion today; competitors have tens of trillions in assets. There is no reason we can't grow substantially. Retirement is a large opportunity, banking and crypto are multiples of that, international and B2B add more. We have a ten-year roadmap; if we execute, we have a compelling opportunity.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Ahmed?
AHMED (Analyst): Vlad and Shiv, congrats on a great quarter. I have noticed strong engagement: AUM almost $400 billion, Gold attach at 17%, all-time high Gold subscribers. Why do you think engagement is becoming so strong? Why are customers adopting credit card, agentic services, trying out meme coins on Robinhood Chain? What about the flywheel is working and how do you sustain it for the next ten years?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): Products have to be good. The credit card has a strong value proposition: 3% cash back on all categories, great UI and virtual cards. Not everything worked perfectly before; we iterated on earlier versions of debit and cash management. We have a flywheel: a customer becomes a Gold subscriber, discovers many products, and if the products are competitive they adopt them. If we get direct deposit, a decent chunk of earnings flows into Robinhood and customers use us for many financial needs. The hard problem is orchestrating all these products coherently and putting the right products in front of the right customers at the right times. As the app evolves, orchestration becomes harder and a key focus area. Each product must be world class individually, and the stitching must be excellent.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. We have more people on the phone, so we'll shift to the Zoom Q&A. First from Zoom: Steven Chubak from Wolfe.
STEVEN CHUBAK (Analyst (Wolfe Research)): Hi. Good evening, Vladimir and Shiv, and thanks for taking my question. Sorry I could not be there in person. On the updated expense guidance: at the start of the year you guided to 18% expense growth with about 10% for new product launches, 5% to support the core, and 3% for acquisitions. How have those buckets evolved under the new guidance and does it still contemplate similar levels of investment in nascent growth initiatives?
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): Great question. The exciting part is we are able to self-fund a lot of growth initiatives. We are still growing and remain a growth company, but because we run lean and disciplined we can self-fund many initiatives. The savings in the outlook come from all three buckets: some from M&A efficiencies, some from the core business teams operating more efficiently, and some from the new initiatives where we are funding more from internal cash flow. The new M&A was not included in the prior outlook but we are self-funding those costs. The teams are delivering fast and efficiently. We have actually added some investments relative to where we started, but overall we are trending well and the lean, disciplined nature is showing through, so we lowered the outlook.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Thank you, Shiv. Next question is from Craig Siegenthaler at Bank of America.
CRAIG SIEGENTHALER (Analyst (Bank of America)): Vlad, Shiv: congrats on the MAS license in Singapore and you also have two small brokerages live in Indonesia. Where are you in the product rollout in Asia? What will the rollout look like relative to the U.S. offering, and what countries can you passport into from Singapore?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): To clarify, this is for our centralized offerings. With the chain and DeFi offerings, we are live in many countries already. For centralized brokerage, we got approval in Singapore and are working to bring everything permissible by MAS. From lessons in the U.K., it is better to launch with a fuller set of capabilities rather than incremental launches. We are trying to bring more of the ecosystem live at launch in Singapore. We anticipate Singapore to be our APAC hub and we can passport from there into many countries in the region; in some countries like Indonesia we will pursue direct licensure where it makes sense to go deeper locally.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): Thank you. Next: Alexander Markgraff at KeyBanc.
ALEXANDER MARKGRAFF (Analyst (KeyBanc)): Thanks. On Robinhood Chain and DeFi expansion, how does engaging customers with on-chain products change how you interact with and capture customers? And Shiv, from a monetization standpoint, how should we think about those relationships versus current C5 relationships?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): On engagement, many of those customers are active on social platforms and listen to podcasts; we see no problem building for those channels. We'll adapt our outreach and content where our customers are active. We are exploring many channels to ensure the products meet customers where they are.
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): From monetization: per transaction, we make a few basis points — not per volume, per transaction — and it varies by size and asset. We share roughly half of revenues with Arbitrum as the L2 we built on top of. As the business scales, we will break down more specifics, but think of it as a few basis points on transactions with a roughly 50% revenue share to the Layer 2 partner in these early stages.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Thank you. Next: Brian Bedell at Deutsche Bank.
BRIAN BEDELL (Analyst (Deutsche Bank)): Brett. Thanks. My question is on Rothera and the company financial KPI with Cboe filing to launch these potentially in the near term. What is the interest in Rothera launching these, and how are you thinking about migrating more event contract activity at Robinhood to Rothera, such as NFL markets?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): My understanding is some filings are under securities-based regimes, and Rothera may not be launching those specific products. Robinhood can connect to a wide range of counterparties through our brokerage and FCM businesses, and Rothera is a great joint venture with SIG. Regardless, the products are useful and there is interest. In the near to medium term, you should expect a growing portion of flow to go through Rothera as it scales. After one month, Rothera is already doing tremendous volume and we will continue to scale it.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Thank you. Next: Patrick Moley at Piper Sandler.
PATRICK MOLEY (Analyst (Piper Sandler)): Hi, guys. Vladimir, I want to follow up on perps in the U.S. You submitted a comment letter supporting CFTC allowing perps and others have launched or are moving in that direction. Why are you not being more aggressive in launching perps in the U.S.? Are you worried about leverage, cannibalization, or is this a deliberate choice to let others take regulatory first-mover risk?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): We are not hesitant about perps. We have many product opportunities and are executing on many fronts. We have perps live overseas via both our DeFi offerings and centralized venues. The absence of a public near-term timeline on an earnings call should not be read as lack of intent. We intend to offer perps to customers and are making progress with regulators; we prefer to avoid committing to specific timelines here.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Next: Benjamin Budish at Barclays.
BENJAMIN BUDISH (Analyst (Barclays)): Hey, good evening. Thanks for taking the question. Shiv, could you unpack the July commentary a little more? You said ADV was trending similar to Q2. On a product-by-product basis, are equities and options similar to Q2? And can you give color on take rate, which can bounce around, particularly for options? Crypto wasn't included in that commentary — any color there? Also, what drove the fee rate improvement in Q2 and what are you seeing in Q3?
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): Sure. For July, ADVs for equities, options, and prediction markets are all in a similar area to Q2 — healthy engagement across those. Crypto is a little slower than what we saw in Q2, but it is early in the month. For take rates in July, they are in a similar area to the Q2 average, and that is a reasonable starting point. Fee rates are an output metric influenced by mix shifts, volatility, contract types, and for crypto, institutional tiers. There are many moving pieces, but big picture July is in the same ZIP code for take rates compared to Q2 averages for most asset classes.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Thank you. Next: Edward Engel at Compass Point.
EDWARD ENGEL (Analyst (Compass Point)): Hey, guys. Thanks for taking my question. You are focused on bringing more volume to Rothera, but there have been reports of exploring partnerships with other exchanges. Do you see opportunities to improve your economics by partnering with different exchanges, or is the focus more on bringing activity under Rothera?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): It is both. We are invested in Rothera and plan to push more flow there, but we also connect to other counterparties. Historically we've connected to ForecastEx, Kalshi, and now Rothera. We always evaluate opportunities to diversify and make sure customers have access to multiple options and we are not reliant on any single counterparty.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Next: Andrew Hardy at BTIG.
ANDREW HARDY (Analyst (BTIG)): Hey Vlad and Shiv. Thanks for taking the question. Sorry I can't be there in person — my wife's due next week, so congrats. I am looking forward to setting up the trust account. You mentioned top-of-funnel: what areas are you focusing on for customer acquisition going forward? Second, did you see any benefit in the quarter from elimination of the pattern day trading rule and are you doing anything to draw back customers who might have left in the past?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): Top-of-funnel work includes improving onboarding, especially as customers can sign up for multiple accounts and assets; we are investing in that. We are also studying how to use the card and banking as drivers: can cardholders be converted into brokerage customers and vice versa? There is a lot of opportunity we haven't fully explored yet. (With best wishes on the upcoming birth!)
SHIV KUMAR VERMA (CFO): Regarding the pattern day trading rule removal: we are pleased the SEC removed that antiquated rule which penalized small-balance customers. It was a nice tailwind in June when the rule went through and it benefits customers across the industry. We likely had an outsized benefit given our customer base. Customers are continuing to come back and adopt trading again; we are seeing it in NPS surveys and other measures that customers who had left are pleased they are allowed to trade again.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. Next: Gav from Wolfe Research on Zoom.
GAV (Analyst (Wolfe Research)): Hey Vlad and Shiv. Great to see you. Wanted to talk about AI agents and agentic trading. This is one of the most fascinating things you've rolled out. I have already hooked it up with Claude and I can see it driving additional volumes. What milestones are you looking for with agentic trading, and do you think it could truly increase volumes beyond human trading? Also, will Agentic trading access prediction markets?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): On the product side, the goal is to give agents access to all the tools a human trader can use on Robinhood where it makes sense. Historically Robinhood was more closed; now we are opening up carefully. The team has been cooking on Agentic features and there is much more to come. We look forward to sharing more, including at the active trader event coming up. Regarding prediction markets, the plan is to expand Agentic access to more products over time where appropriate and permitted.
CHRIS KOEGEL (VP of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations): All right. We will finish strong. Vladimir, any closing remarks?
VLADIMIR TENEV (Chairman and CEO): First, thank you for all the engagement from institutional, sell-side, retail, and content creators. I am proud of the community that has coalesced around the company. The team has been working incredibly hard. The roadmap is full and there is a lot to do. I hope to see some of you at the next Hood Summit in Houston, Texas. Thank you.
